section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Binary
section_1.content: Briefly introduce the binary system (base-2). Explain how binary digits (0 and 1) represent positions: the rightmost bit is 2^0, the next is 2^1, etc. Visual: A row of 3 light bulbs turning on/off to represent the numbers 0-7.

section_2.title: The Towers of Hanoi Rules
section_2.content: Introduce the puzzle: 3 rods and N disks of different sizes. Rules: Only one disk moved at a time, no larger disk can sit on a smaller one. Visual: A 3-disk stack transitioning through states.
section_2.example: A monk moving 3 golden disks from Rod A to Rod C.

section_3.title: Mapping Binary to Moves
section_3.content: The core revelation: The step number (1 to 2^n - 1) in binary reveals which disk to move. Disk 1 (the smallest) moves every odd step; Disk 2 moves every 2 steps; Disk 3 every 4 steps. Visual: A binary counter ticking alongside the movement of the disks.
section_3.example: Step 3 (binary 011): The '1' in the 2nd position tells us to move Disk 2.

section_4.title: Visualizing the Pattern
section_4.content: Demonstrate the synchronization between the binary counter and the disk movement. Highlight that the total number of moves for n disks is 2^n - 1, which corresponds to the binary number consisting of n ones.
section_4.example: For 3 disks, the total moves = 2^3 - 1 = 7 steps (binary 111).

section_5.title: Real-World Application
section_5.content: Conclude by connecting this to recursive algorithms in computing. Binary counting acts as the 'map' for the algorithm to navigate the state space efficiently without backtracking.
section_5.example: A robotic arm programmed to solve physical puzzles using an internal binary clock.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Binary logic models recursive algorithms.", "It navigates complex state spaces efficiently.", "Robotic arms use binary clocks precisely."]
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        memory_grid = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.5, color=WHITE) for _ in range(9)]).arrange_in_grid(3, 3)
        self.place_in_area(memory_grid, 'A2', 'C4')

        stack_chart = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=1, height=0.3, color=RED) for _ in range(4)]).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(stack_chart, 'D2', 'F4')

        robot_icon = Circle(radius=0.5, color=BLUE).add(Dot(color=BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(robot_icon, 'E5')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(memory_grid))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(stack_chart))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(robot_icon))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#0000FF")
        self.wait(2)
